elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Revised § 2.1 reads: "Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment." This replaces the prior USD 2,000,000/year three-year take-or-pay obligation and is consistent with § 12.3 ("Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment").

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained § 7.1: "Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form ... unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify." Fees are defined as amounts payable under an Order Form, so payment is limited to ordered Services or usage-priced items.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no commitment survives after § 2.1 is replaced with an express no-minimum-commitment statement, so there is nothing to limit to a 12-month term. The fallback checklist is moot because the preferred (stronger) outcome is achieved.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment remaining in § 2.1, there is no commitment requiring a reduction right. The margin comment offers this fallback only if Vendor insists on a commitment.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no shortfall mechanic, take-or-pay formula, or penalty remains anywhere in the cited language after § 2.1 is replaced; § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: § 2.1 as rendered is an unconditional statement that Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment, and retained § 7.1 confines payment to Fees stated in each Order Form (usage-priced where the Order Form so provides) while barring unidentified minimum-use charges.

Minimal: only § 2.1 was rewritten, and the replacement is a concise substitute for the offending take-or-pay sentence. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or extra requirements were added; §§ 7.1 and 12.3 are retained verbatim and no Customer-favourable wording elsewhere was deleted.

Preserves intent: the Fees, Order Form, and Services definitions and the payment mechanics in § 7.1 continue to operate; removing the take-or-pay obligation leaves no dangling cross-reference, undefined trigger, or contradictory retained sentence, and it resolves the prior conflict with § 12.3's acknowledgement of no minimum-volume commitment.
No residual shortfall, instalment, or contingent payment formula remains, so the deletion is unconditional rather than merely narrowed.

Fallback elements are recorded as met only because their condition (an existing commitment) no longer applies; if Vendor insists on reinstating a commitment, the drafter must then add the 12-month limit, the 30-day reduction right, and an express true-up in operative text rather than in the margin comment.
